meta.title: Kiln Yoga, small yoga classes above a bakery in Peckham
meta.description: Slow flow, yin, a 4 week beginners course and Saturday pregnancy yoga in a warm wooden room in Peckham. Only 14 mats. Book a single class or a pass.

rationale: A kiln is orange and so is a loaf of bread, so the page is printed in two colours: baked terracotta and deep navy, like a screen-printed class poster pinned to the bakery door. Young Serif gives the headlines a handmade, slightly wobbly warmth, and the 14 mats become the visual hook (a drawn floor plan of the room, a stamp, a marquee). Compositions stay unhurried and low-key in the middle (a big numbered class list, a letter from Mei, a question and answer about starting) so it feels like the room and not like a gym.

items.name: Slow flow
items.description: Movement linked to the breath, at a pace where you can still feel each shape. Most of the week's timetable.

items.name: Yin
items.description: Long holds on the floor, a few shapes per class. The quiet one, good after a hard week.

items.name: Beginners course
items.description: Four weeks with the same small group in the same room, so nobody is guessing what the others know.

items.name: Pregnancy yoga
items.description: Saturday mornings, gentle and slow, with room to rest whenever you need to.

props.caption: The studio from above: the teacher's mat at the front, fourteen mats on the boards, windows along the top wall, loaves on the shelves of the bakery downstairs.

paragraphs: I teach most of the classes at Kiln, and two other teachers cover the rest. The studio is up a flight of stairs above a bakery in Peckham. On a morning class the whole room smells of bread.
There are 14 mats and I will not squeeze in a fifteenth. That way I can see everyone, and you can come in on a day when you are not sure about yourself and nobody will mind.
The floor is wood, the windows are big and the room is warm. Bring a water bottle. I will lend you a mat if you do not have one.
props.name: Mei

pairs.ask: I have never done yoga. Where do I start?
pairs.answer: The 4 week beginners course. Same small group, same room, and each week adds a little to the last.

pairs.ask: I am pregnant. Is there a class for me?
pairs.answer: Yes, pregnancy yoga runs on Saturday mornings. Slow, gentle, with plenty of time to sit down.

pairs.ask: Do I have to sign up for months?
pairs.answer: No. You can book a single class, or buy a class pass if you know you will keep coming back.

pairs.ask: I just want to switch off for an hour.
pairs.answer: Try yin. Few shapes, long holds, and nobody will ask you to do anything clever.

factsToConfirm.fact: Street address (Rye Lane, Peckham, SE15 is a placeholder)
Class times: weekday evenings 6:30pm, Saturday pregnancy yoga in the morning, Sunday yin late morning
Studio is on the first floor, reached by stairs from a street door next to the bakery, with a bell, shoes off at the top
Mats can be borrowed from the studio
Bakery smell is strongest in the mornings and the studio is lit by big windows along one wall
Yin is described as few shapes with long holds; slow flow as linked to the breath; the beginners course has the same group each week
The 14 mats are laid out in two rows of seven; the floor plan drawing is illustrative
Mei will never add a fifteenth mat
Classes are bookable as singles or with a class pass, with no longer commitment required
